transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-07-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Helios Lead Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Helios Security), Marcus Bennett (Product)

[00:00] Ethan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:04] Jordan (Helios): Jordan here.
[00:06] Sofia (Helios): Sofia.
[00:07] Marcus (Helios): Marcus, yep.
[00:09] Priya (Redwood): Priya here, will do the deep dive into the SDKs and Optimize knobs.
[00:13] Ethan (Redwood): Great. Agenda we sent — 1) quick console walk, 2) Python/TS SDK quickstart, 3) auth patterns and CI rotation, 4) Optimize recommendations for your ingestion workload, 5) next steps. Any additions?
[00:22] Marcus (Helios): Maybe spend a few minutes on dedicated vs hosted — our compliance team is leaning private but cost is a huge concern.
[00:26] Ethan (Redwood): Yep we'll cover that.

Summary + early notes:
[00:35] Ethan (Redwood): Ok quick demo — logging into the Redwood Console, sandbox project. (screen share noise) you should see a project called "helios-sandbox" under our demo org. There's a pre-provisioned API key and service role.
[00:48] Jordan (Helios): I see it. That API key — is it scoped? can we restrict to model/inference only?
[00:52] Priya (Redwood): Yes, keys are policy scoped. You can scope by model, by route, and optionally by allowed origins. For CI we recommend a short-lived service token with rotation via GitHub Actions or your secrets manager.
[01:05] Sofia (Helios): For rotation — do you support KMS integration or HSM? We need to show key material isn't persistent in Redwood.
[01:11] Priya (Redwood): Yes KMS integrations are supported for Private deployments and dedicated customers you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM-backed KMS; hosted supports envelope encryption to customer-managed KMS in supported clouds. There's a doc in the security pack I'll share. (brief pause)

SDK Install (hands-on)
[01:28] Priya (Redwood): Let's jump into the Python quickstart. I'm going to open the repo — simple pip install redwood-inference, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your .env or CI secret. Example code snippet: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']); response = client.generate(...).
[01:44] Jordan (Helios): Any gotchas with async vs sync APIs? We run event-driven workers so async is preferable.
[01:49] Priya (Redwood): We expose both sync and async clients. For high qps we recommend the async client with connection pooling; also, reuse the KV cache across requests in batch processors to avoid re-priming latency.
[02:05] Ethan (Redwood): Quick TypeScript note — npm i @redwood/inference, import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'; new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
[02:18] Marcus (Helios): When you say KV cache reuse — how fragile is that across containers? we autoscale pods.
[02:24] Priya (Redwood): Good question. For autoscaling we recommend sticky routing within a short window or using Redis-backed shared prefix cache we provide on Dedicated. For hosted, we do automatic prefix caching at the edge but for very bursty autoscaling, Dedicated gives more predictable cold-start behavior.

Auth & CI rotation patterns
[02:40] Ethan (Redwood): Walkthrough of recommended secret rotation: create short-lived service token via console, store in GitHub Actions secrets, rotate monthly and automate fetch via OIDC where possible. Example GH action uses the redwood/scripts/get_token script to fetch ephemeral token.
[02:58] Sofia (Helios): Do you support SAML/SSO for access to the console and role-based RBAC? compliance needs that.
[03:04] Priya (Redwood): Yes SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning. RBAC supports route-level and environment-level roles; we'll share the RBAC matrix.

Console: routes, logs, and traces
[03:18] Ethan (Redwood): Showing the console's route config — you can pin model versions, add fallback models, and set a rollout percentage. Also the tracing tab shows per-token latency histograms and per-route cost.
[03:29] Jordan (Helios): Can we export logs to our Splunk/Datadog?
[03:32] Priya (Redwood): Yes log forwarders and S3 export for raw request logs. Audit logs are write-once and available for Dedicated/Private tiers.

Optimize recommendations (live)
[03:45] Priya (Redwood): Based on the sample workload you shared (long-form doc summarization, average input length ~1.2k tokens, peak qps ~18), our recommendations: 1) use batching with max tokens per batch ~2k, 2) enable prefix KV cache for repeated document headers, 3) try a 4-bit quantized variant of the model for cost-sensitive paths. We'll attach a benchmark matrix.
[04:05] Marcus (Helios): How much latency hit with quantization?
[04:08] Priya (Redwood): Usually 5-15% median latency increase depending on model/hardware, but cost reductions can be 30-60%. We can run a 2-hour bench on your sample corpus to show numbers.
[04:19] Jordan (Helios): That would help. Our SLO is 200ms P95 for short responses, but many of our tasks are long-form so 500-800ms is tolerable for batch jobs.

Technical deep dive snippets
[04:35] Priya (Redwood): For high-throughput synchronous low-latency, Dedicated with pinned model shards on A100/RTX-class hardware gives the best consistency. Hosted has regional fallbacks and autoscaling but can show variance under cold starts. You can set routing policy to prefer Dedicated when available and fall back to hosted if Dedicated saturated.
[04:56] Sofia (Helios): If we go Private (VPC), do we still get the same Console UX?
[04:59] Ethan (Redwood): Yes. The control plane remains the same; for Private we deploy a control-plane connector in your VPC and the UI talks to your deployment. Audit logs and KMS integration remain intact. There are some setup steps for network egress and service endpoints.

Objections & cost discussion
[05:20] Marcus (Helios): Cost is big. If we run high-volume summarization during batch jobs, what's the rough unit cost delta between hosted and dedicated?
[05:27] Priya (Redwood): Ballpark — hosted is higher per-token due to multi-tenant overhead; Dedicated with reserved capacity and batching tends to be 30-50% cheaper at scale. Optimize features (caching + quantization) can push savings further. We'll put concrete numbers in the benchmark sheet specific to your model choice.
[05:42] Jordan (Helios): Another question — data retention. We cannot keep customer prompts. Does Redwood persist input data?
[05:47] Ethan (Redwood): By default hosted keeps short-term logs for troubleshooting (30 days) but you can opt-out and disable retention. Dedicated/Private gives explicit controls and logs can be forwarded or disabled. We have a data processing addendum for enterprise.

Live troubleshooting & code run
[06:05] Priya (Redwood): Ok let's run a quick sample in the Python sandbox. (typing) Using the async client, sending a 600-token prompt, enabling streaming. Response arrives, small overlap in transcription: "uh" and filler. 
[06:28] Jordan (Helios): Looks good. For TS we want to call from Cloud Functions — any warmup recommendations?
[06:33] Priya (Redwood): For serverless, use a light warming process or prefer batch post-processing patterns. Or use a tiny dedicated pool to front requests; we can recommend autoscale configs.

Shared artifacts mentioned
[06:50] Ethan (Redwood): I'll drop the quickstart repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (sandbox branch) and the security pack: https://redwood.ai/security/pack.pdf. Also the benchmark template: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/helios-template.xlsx

Questions from customer
[07:10] Sofia (Helios): Does audit logging include prompt text or only metadata?
[07:14] Priya (Redwood): It depends on retention settings; you can redact prompts at ingestion or route logs to your S3 and control retention yourself. We'll include recommended log filters.
[07:24] Marcus (Helios): For the pilot, can we have burst capacity? sometimes we spike for end-of-day jobs.
[07:29] Ethan (Redwood): Yes — Dedicated has burst lanes and flexible autoscaling policies; we can scope that in the pilot commitment. Hosted has automatic bursting but less guaranteed QOS.

Wrap-up and recap
[07:45] Ethan (Redwood): To recap — we'll provide a sandbox org with scoped API keys, quickstart code for py/ts, benchmark sheet and Optimize suggestions, and a security pack. Customer will confirm pilot scope and SLOs.
[07:57] Jordan (Helios): Sounds good. Sofia: any final security blockers?
[08:00] Sofia (Helios): I need to see SOC2 type II and the KMS integration guide. Also a diagram for data flow in Private deployment.
[08:06] Ethan (Redwood): We'll include those.

Final minutes: next scheduling
[08:12] Ethan (Redwood): Let's pencil pilot kickoff for Monday 2025-07-21 at 16:00 UTC unless you prefer earlier.
[08:18] Jordan (Helios): Works for me.
[08:20] Marcus (Helios): Works.
[08:21] Sofia (Helios): OK.
[08:22] Priya (Redwood): I'll also schedule a 30-minute dedicated performance deep-dive after initial bench results.

[58:00] Meeting ended

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had a few misattributed labels; we've preserved filler words and some run-on sentences. Some product names were picked up imperfectly (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes shown as "K V cache").
notes: This is a sales-led demo with AE+SE. The transcript contains natural speech artifacts and imperfect transcription as typical. Shared links noted for quickstart and security pack.
